blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: End-to-end driving models perform well on standard benchmarks but collide frequently in safety-critical scenarios. We present a failure-mode analysis on NeuroNCAP which shows that 95.9% of DiffusionDrive's collisions are planning failures despite reliable detection, pinpointing the bottleneck in planning rather than perception. We attribute this to a fundamental data imbalance, as safety-critical interactions are rare in real driving logs, so planners are hardly ever trained on them. We close this gap with a novel model-aware framework that generates safety-critical training scenes against a specific planner. Each planner is attacked at the bird's-eye-view (BEV) level through a differentiable surrogate distilled from its own planning head. This keeps the expensive video renderer out of the attack loop. We extract 50 scenes per planner, each pairing an attack with a safe escape trajectory that serves as the fine-tuning label. A fully automated quality-diversity search generates both the attacks and the escapes, so that their variety is not specified by hand. Only these scenes are rendered to fine-tune the planner, which reduces the computational cost significantly. Fine-tuning on these scenes roughly halves the closed-loop collision rate of two planners on NeuroNCAP (SparseDrive 28.0% to 12.2%, DiffusionDrive 37.5% to 19.2%) while largely preserving normal driving. A cross-planner transfer experiment shows that the gain comes from targeting the specific planner. Each planner improves most on the scenes generated against itself, and DiffusionDrive fine-tuned on SparseDrive's scenes retains only 6.7 of its 18.3-point collision-rate reduction.
blocks.zh: 端到端驱动模型在标准基准方面表现良好,但在安全关键情况下经常相撞。 我们提出了NeuroNCAP的故障模式分析, 显示95.9%的Drive相撞是计划失败, 尽管可靠的检测, 我们将此归因于一个基本的数据不平衡,因为安全-关键相互作用在真正的驱动日志中是罕见的,因此规划者几乎没有受过这方面的培训. 我们用一个新颖的模型认识框架来弥补这一差距,这个框架产生针对具体规划者的安全关键训练场景。 每个计划者在鸟眼-视野(BEV)级别上通过自规划头部分出不同的代位被攻击. 这使得昂贵的视频渲染器无法进入攻击循环. 我们每个计划员抽取50个场景,每个场景将攻击与安全逃生轨迹配对,作为微调标签. 完全自动化的质量多样性搜索既能产生攻击,又能产生出出出逃,这样它们的种类就不会由手来指定. 只有这些场景才被制成来微调规划师,这大大降低了计算成本. 这些场景的精细调整大致将神经NCAP上两位规划者的闭路相撞率减半(SparseDrive 28.0%至12.2%,Drive 37.5%至19.2%),同时基本保持了正常驾驶. 一个跨计划员转移实验显示,收益来自针对特定计划员. 每个规划师在所生成的自相矛盾的场景上改进得最多,在斯帕塞德里夫的场景上被DifmusionDrive微调后仅保留了其18.3分相撞率降低的6.7.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
End-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving has shown strong performance on standard benchmarks, yet the models are limited by the data they are trained on.
Real-world driving datasets are heavily skewed toward normal, uneventful driving, with safety-critical interactions accounting for less than 0.03% of real-world driving time [ 1 ] . Such situations are inherently rare in naturalistic driving and cannot be deliberately staged at scale for safety, cost, and legal reasons.
As soon as these models encounter scenarios outside their training distribution, performance degrades sharply.
On Challenger, which generates physically plausible videos for adversarial scenarios such as cut-ins, sudden lane changes, and blind-spot intrusions, the collision rate of state-of-the-art E2E models increases by up to 26 × \times compared to standard nuScenes evaluation [ 2 ] .
While Challenger stress-tests models through video-based adversarial replay, NeuroNCAP evaluates in closed-loop, where the ego executes its own plan and failures hidden in open loop appear, on harder scenarios including oncoming vehicles, stationary vehicles, and side collisions [ 3 ] .
There SparseDrive results in a collision rate of 28.0% and DiffusionDrive in 37.5%.
blocks.zh:
端对端(E2E)自主驱动在标准基准上表现出了强劲的性能,然而模型却受到所培训的数据的限制.
真实世界驾驶数据集严重向正常,平稳的驾驶方向倾斜,安全关键互动占真实世界驾驶时间的0.03%以下[1]. 这种情形在自然驾驶中本来就是罕见的,不能出于安全、成本和法律原因故意大规模进行。
一旦这些模型在培训分配之外遇到情景,性能就会急剧下降。
在挑战者号(Challenger)上,它为诸如切入,突然车道变化,盲点入侵等对抗性情况产生物理上可信的视频,与标准nuScenes评价相比,最先进的E2E型号的碰撞率最高增加了26×xxx时间[2].
虽然挑战者压力测试模型通过基于视频的对抗性重播,但NeuronNCAP在闭路评估中,自我执行自己的计划,而隐藏在公开循环中的失败出现,在更难的情景中,包括即将到来的车辆,固定车辆,以及侧面碰撞[3].
那边的 Sparse 驱动器导致28.0%的碰撞率和37.5%的分散驱动率。

blocks.en:
Since collecting safety-critical driving data at scale remains impractical, several directions have been explored to synthetically close this gap.
Video generation models such as MagicDriveV2 [ 4 ] can synthesize photorealistic multi-view driving videos.
Yet they are evaluated almost exclusively on perceptual quality metrics like FID and FVD, and their videos have so far served perception tasks such as 3D detection and tracking [ 5 , 6 ] rather than planning.
Methods that do generate training data for the planner either derive it from validation failures without closed-loop evaluation [ 7 ] or simulate hundreds of thousands of scenes reconstructed from logged drives [ 8 ] .
In both cases the scenarios come from existing data rather than being designed as interactions.
Adversarial scenario generation designs such interactions deliberately, but either at the state level without photorealistic rendering [ 9 , 10 , 11 ] or, as in Challenger [ 2 ] , against the logged ego trajectory rather than against a planner.
No existing method generates photorealistic adversarial scenes optimized against a specific vision-based planner.
blocks.zh:
由于大规模收集安全关键驱动数据仍然是不切实际的,因此已经探索了几个方向来综合缩小这一差距。
MagicDriveV2[4]等视频生成模型可以合成光现实主义多视图驱动视频.
然而,它们几乎完全依靠诸如FID和FVD等感知性质量衡量标准来评估,而其视频迄今为止为3D检测和跟踪[5,6]等感知任务服务,而不是计划.
为规划者生成培训数据的方法要么来自未经闭路评价的验证失败[7],要么模拟从记录的驱动器重建的数十万场景[8]。
在这两种情况下,设想方案都来自现有数据,而不是作为互动设计。
反常的情景生成设计这种相互作用是故意的,但要么在州一级没有光现实化渲染[9,10,11],要么像挑战者[2]中那样,与记录的自我轨迹相对立,而不是与计划者相对立.
任何现有方法都不会产生光现实主义的对抗场景,这些场景是针对一个基于特定视觉的规划者而优化的.

blocks.en:
To locate the bottleneck behind these E2E failures, we decompose every closed-loop collision on NeuroNCAP into a perception or a planning failure by checking whether the planner detected and tracked the adversary.
In 95.9% of DiffusionDrive’s collisions, the threat is detected, so the model sees the danger but fails to react.
Targeting this weakness with generated scenes requires the gradient of a collision objective with respect to the adversary’s behavior.
For a vision-based planner, whose input is rendered video, this gradient would have to pass through the video renderer, which is computationally infeasible.
We therefore attack a surrogate instead.
We distill the target planner π \pi into a differentiable surrogate planner π ^ \hat{\pi} , which consists of the planner’s own planning head, copied and frozen, behind a small trained adapter that takes ground-truth bird’s-eye-view (BEV) state instead of images.
The failure analysis justifies this construction, since perception is reliable.
Gradients through π ^ \hat{\pi} are cheap and point at the planner’s specific failure modes rather than at a generic driving prior.
Every generated scene is therefore optimized against the planner to be fine-tuned.
blocks.zh:
为了找到这些E2E故障背后的瓶颈,我们通过检查计划者是否检测到并跟踪对手,将NeuronNCAP上每一次闭路碰撞都分解成感知或计划失败.
在95.9%的DiffusionDrive碰撞中,检测到威胁,所以模型看到危险但未能反应.
以产生的场景来对付这一弱点需要敌方行为的碰撞目标的梯度。
对于一个以视觉为基础的规划器,其输入是视频,这种梯度必须经过视频渲染器,这在计算上是不可行的。
因此,我们攻击代孕者。
我们把目标规划师 \\pi 蒸馏成一个不同的替代规划师 \\\ \\ \ \ \ \ \ 由规划师自己的规划负责人组成, 复制和冻结, 在一个训练有素的小型适配器后面,
失败分析为这种解释提供了理由,因为感觉是可靠的。
通过 ^\ \ \ \ \ \ pi} 的渐进方式是便宜的, 并且指向规划者的具体失败模式, 而不是一个通用的驱动方式。
因此,每个生成的场景都会与规划师进行优化,以进行微调.

blocks.en:
Those gradients drive the attack search, steering an adversarial vehicle in BEV to maximize collision risk for the planner.
A quality-diversity search spreads the attacks over different behaviors, so the types of attack are found by the search rather than specified by hand.
A geometric solver then computes a safe escape trajectory for every scene as its fine-tuning label and rejects scenes for which no escape exists.
The search costs around 30 GPU-hours per planner, and only the 50 surviving scenes are later rendered photorealistically.
We evaluate closed-loop on NeuroNCAP, open-loop on Challenger’s adversarial replay, and on clean nuScenes to confirm that fine-tuning does not degrade normal driving.
These 50 scenes roughly halve each planner’s closed-loop collision rate on NeuroNCAP (SparseDrive 28.0% to 12.2%, DiffusionDrive 37.5% to 19.2%; Fig. 1 ) while normal driving is largely preserved.
blocks.zh:
这些梯度带动了攻击搜索,引导BEV的对抗飞行器,以尽量增大计划者碰撞的风险.
质量多样性的搜索将攻击传播到不同的行为上,所以攻击的类型是由搜索找到的,而不是用手指定的.
几何解析器然后计算每个场景的安全逃逸轨迹作为它的微调标签,并拒绝不存在逃逸的场景.
搜索费用为每名规划师大约30GPU小时左右,后来只有50场幸存的场景才以摄影现实化的方式制作.
我们评价NeuronNCAP的闭路,挑战者对抗性的重播的闭路,以及清洁的nuScens,以确认微调不会降低正常驾驶。
这50幕大致将每个规划者在神经NCAP(SparseDrive 28.0%至12.2%,Drive 37.5%至19.2%;图1)上的闭路碰撞率减半,而正常驾驶则基本保留下来。

blocks.en: In short, our contributions are: • A failure-mode analysis on NeuroNCAP showing that 95.9% of DiffusionDrive’s closed-loop collisions are planning failures despite reliable detection, which motivates fine-tuning the planning head only. • A novel differentiable surrogate of a vision-based E2E planner, built from the planner’s own frozen planning head behind a small adapter over ground-truth BEV state and validated against the real planner. • To our knowledge, the first model-aware pipeline for generating photorealistic safety-critical scenes for vision-based E2E planners. It optimizes attacks through the surrogate with a quality-diversity search, labels each scene with a geometrically solved escape, and rejects scenes for which no escape exists. With 50 scenes per planner, it roughly halves the closed-loop collision rate of two planners. • A cross-planner transfer experiment showing that each planner improves most on the scenes generated against itself, and that this benefit is larger for DiffusionDrive than for SparseDrive. The gain therefore comes from targeting the specific planner rather than from adversarial data in general. We will release the code, the distilled surrogates, and the generated adversarial scenes for both planners.
blocks.zh: 简而言之,我们的贡献是: – 对NeuroNCAP的失败模式分析显示,95.9%的DifunusionDrive闭路碰撞是计划失败的,尽管有可靠的检测结果,而这只刺激了计划头的微调。 · 一个不同小说中的E2E规划器的替代器,该规划器是从规划器本身的冷冻规划头部建造的,位于地面真实BEV状态的小型适应器后面,并与真正的规划器相对应。 据我们所知,是第一个为基于视觉的E2E规划者制作光现实安全关键场景的模型-认识管道。 它以质量多样性搜索优化通过代位攻击,将每个场景贴上几何解脱的标签,并拒绝不存在逃脱的场景. 每个计划员50幕, 大约将两个计划员的闭路碰撞率减半。 • 支助 一个跨计划员转移实验显示,每个计划员在反自身生成的场景上改进最多,这种好处对于DivusionDrive比SparseDrive更大. 因此,收益来自针对具体的规划者,而不是一般的对抗性数据。 我们将发布代码, 蒸馏代孕, 和产生的对抗场景 两个规划者。

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en:
End-to-End Autonomous Driving. End-to-end driving models map raw sensor observations directly to planning actions, bypassing modular pipelines [ 12 ] .
Recent planners include imitation-based architectures [ 13 , 14 ] , diffusion-based planners that model multimodal trajectory distributions [ 15 ] , and trajectory scoring approaches [ 16 ] .
Strong scores on standard benchmarks [ 17 ] say little about their behavior in rare interactions, and since such interactions barely appear in real logs [ 1 ] , the training data cannot correct this on its own.
blocks.zh:
端对端自主驾驶. 端对端驱动模型将原始传感器观测直接映射到规划动作,绕过模块化管道[12].
近期的规划者包括基于模仿的架构[13,14],以传播为基础的规划者,模拟多式联运轨迹分布[15],以及轨迹评分方法[16].
标准基准的强分[17]很少提到他们在稀有相互作用中的行为,由于这种相互作用很少出现在真实的日志[1]中,因此训练数据本身无法纠正这一点.

blocks.en:
Adversarial Scenario Generation. Several methods optimize traffic scenarios against a planner.
STRIVE [ 9 ] perturbs the latents of a learned traffic prior until a rule-based planner crashes, SAFE-SIM [ 10 ] guides trajectory diffusion with collision costs, CTG++ [ 18 ] steers scene-level diffusion with loss functions derived from language queries, CAT [ 19 ] runs closed-loop adversarial training in state-level simulation, AdvSim [ 20 ] perturbs actor trajectories and re-simulates LiDAR sweeps, and KING [ 11 ] obtains attack gradients through a kinematic proxy of the simulator dynamics in CARLA.
More recent methods steer language models or learned motion priors toward critical interactions [ 21 , 22 ] .
All of these act at the state or LiDAR level against rule-based, privileged, or simulator-native planners, and none renders its attacks photorealistically for a vision-based planner.
Our adversary is instead optimized against the deployed vision-based planner itself, through a distilled surrogate of its own planning head.
The resulting scenes reach that planner as photorealistic video.

blocks.en:
Generative Driving Data and Photorealistic Evaluation. Generative video models expand driving data distributions, from structured-controllability work [ 23 , 6 , 24 ] to MagicDriveV2 [ 4 ] , which synthesizes high-resolution multi-camera video with fine-grained control over scene layout via 3D bounding boxes and trajectories, making it a suitable backbone for targeted scenario synthesis.
Generated video has mostly served perception tasks, with quality measured by FID and FVD rather than downstream planning.
Delphi [ 7 ] guides generation with validation-set failure patterns, which risks benchmark-specific overfitting and is never evaluated closed-loop. SimScale [ 8 ] improves planner robustness through sim-real co-training on 147K recovery-based simulated scenes reconstructed from logged drives rather than designed as interactions.
On the evaluation side, NeuroNCAP [ 3 ] tests vision-based planners closed-loop in neurally rendered collision scenarios and Challenger [ 2 ] renders adversarial video for open-loop stress testing, and we adopt both as benchmarks.
blocks.zh:
基因驱动数据和光现实性评价。 基因视频模型扩展了驱动数据分布,从结构控制工作[23,6,24]到MagicDriveV2[4],它通过3D边框和轨迹合成高分辨率多镜头视频,对场景布局进行精细控制,使其成为目标情景合成的合适骨干.
制作的视频大多服务于感知任务,质量由FID和FVD衡量,而不是下游规划.
Delphi [7] 以验证-设定的失败模式指导生成,这有可能使特定基准过于适应,并且从未被评价为闭路. SimScale [8] 通过对147K恢复模拟场景进行模拟真实的共训,改进了规划员的稳健性,这些场景是从记录的驱动器重建而来,而不是设计成相互作用的.
在评价方面,NeuronNCAP[3]测试基于视觉的规划者在神经学中闭锁-闭锁使碰撞场景,挑战者[2]将对抗视频作为开放-闭锁压力测试,我们同时采用两者作为基准.

blocks.en:
Attacking a substitute model is standard in adversarial machine learning, where transferability across models is well documented but partial [ 25 ] , and STRIVE’s rule-based proxy planner is the scenario-generation analogue.
Our surrogate is not a generic proxy, as it reuses the target’s own frozen planning head. So its gradients are specific to that planner, and our transfer experiment measures the effect of that specificity.
To our knowledge, this is the first work to distill a vision-based end-to-end planner into a differentiable surrogate and generate its own training attacks through it.
blocks.zh:
攻击替代模式是对抗性机器学习中的标准,在这种模式中,跨模式的可转移性有详细记录,但部分[25],而STRIVE的基于规则的代理规划者是情景生成模拟.
我们的代孕不是一般的代名词, 因此,它的梯度是针对那个规划者的, 我们的转移实验测量了这种特异性的效果。

blocks.en: III Method
blocks.zh: 三、结 论 方法

blocks.en:
A vision-based end-to-end planner π \pi maps surround-view images through a perception module to context features c c , which a planning head f head f_{\mathrm{head}} decodes into the ego trajectory τ \tau .
Given a trained π \pi and real driving logs, we seek a small set of safety-critical training scenes.
Each scene is a photorealistic video of an adversarial vehicle paired with an expert label for the ego’s escape, and fine-tuning π \pi on these scenes should reduce its closed-loop collision rate without degrading normal driving.
The generation of the scenes is model-aware in the sense that every attack is optimized against π \pi ’s own planning head. Thus two different planners receive different safety-critical scenes.
The pipeline runs in four stages (Fig. 2 ): (A) distill π \pi into a differentiable surrogate that plans from ground-truth BEV state, (B) optimize adversarial trajectories through the surrogate under a quality-diversity search, (C) solve a safe escape for every attack and reject scenes that admit none, and (D) render the surviving scenes photorealistically and fine-tune the real planner on them.

blocks.en: III-A Distilling a Differentiable Surrogate

blocks.en:
Optimizing an adversary against the planner π \pi requires the gradient of a collision objective with respect to the adversary’s motion, taken through the planner.
Since π \pi consumes images, that puts the video renderer inside the optimization loop.
Rendering a single scene, a six-camera clip of 65 frames at 12 Hz (5.4 s) and 848×1600 pixels per camera, already costs about 1.4 GPU-hours, one attack needs on the order of sixty renders, and each optimization step would additionally have to differentiate through the video renderer.
Attacking the real planner directly is therefore computationally out of reach. We build a surrogate that maps the BEV state instead of images.

因此,直接攻击真正的规划人员在计算上是无法达到的。 我们建造一个代理设备,来绘制BEV状态而不是图像。

It uses one encoder per input group (agents, map lanes, ego state), and each encoder produces one part of the features c c .

Training data comes from the planner itself.
We run π \pi on nuScenes and record, per sample, the context features c c its perception produces and the trajectory τ \tau its head outputs, while b b is assembled from the same samples’ ground-truth annotations.
Only θ \theta trains using the loss ℒ ( θ ) = λ f ∥ A θ ( b ) − c ∥ 2 2 + λ t ∥ π ^ ( b ) − τ ∥ 2 2 , \mathcal{L}(\theta)=\lambda_{\mathrm{f}}\,\bigl\lVert A_{\theta}(b)-c\bigr\rVert_{2}^{2}\;+\;\lambda_{\mathrm{t}}\,\bigl\lVert\hat{\pi}(b)-\tau\bigr\rVert_{2}^{2}, (2) so the adapter is matched to the head twice, once in the feature space the head reads and once in the trajectory the head produces from those features.

For DiffusionDrive, whose head scores several trajectory modes and executes the best, the mode selection is softened so the forward path stays differentiable.
We validate the construction before any use.
First, we confirm that the extracted head reproduces the real planner’s trajectory when given the recorded features.
Second, the gradient of a distance-to-ego-path objective with respect to the adversary’s controls, computed through the surrogate, is finite and has a similar magnitude across scenes for both planners.
The construction rests on the assumption that ground-truth BEV approximates what the planner actually perceives.
Our failure analysis supports this hypothesis, as 95.9% of DiffusionDrive’s (95.8% of SparseDrive’s) closed-loop collisions occur with perception working (Sec. IV-B ).

blocks.en: III-B Model-Aware Attack Generation
blocks.zh: III-B 模型-智能攻击生成

blocks.en:
An attack is a sequence of controls for one adversarial vehicle, an acceleration a a and a steering angle δ \delta at each of the T T timesteps of the scene.
A kinematic bicycle model unrolls the controls into a trajectory, and replacing the adversary’s original trajectory in b b with it gives the attacked BEV state b ⁡ ( a , δ ) b(a,\delta) .
We minimize a collision objective J ⁡ ( a , δ ) J(a,\delta) by gradient descent on the controls through the bicycle model and the surrogate. J ⁡ ( a , δ ) J(a,\delta) consists of several terms.
The main term draws the adversary toward the ego path that π ^ \hat{\pi} predicts for b ⁡ ( a , δ ) b(a,\delta) .
A timing term forces the attacker and the ego to reach the meeting point at the same time.
Further terms keep the attack on the drivable area, clear of other agents, and within realistic steering, acceleration and jerk.
Optimizing controls rather than positions keeps every attack physically drivable.
The controls for the full horizon are optimized jointly in a single gradient run.
During the run, π ^ \hat{\pi} is evaluated at several frames along the rolled-out trajectory, so the ego’s predicted reaction stays consistent with the attacker’s committed path.
Because π ^ \hat{\pi} re-plans as the adversary moves, the attack is dynamically coupled to what this planner would actually do rather than to a static script.

blocks.en:
A single optimized attack, however, tends to rediscover the same failure.
To cover a planner’s failure modes without hand-picking scenario types, we run the optimization inside MAP-Elites [ 26 ] , a quality-diversity search.
MAP-Elites divides a space of behavior descriptors into a grid and keeps, in each grid cell, the attack that comes physically closest to the ego.
We use two descriptors, contact time-gap and approach angle, on a 5 × 5 5\times 5 grid.
The grid forces the attacks to spread over the descriptor space, while the type of attack in each cell, such as a cut-in or a head-on approach, is not specified and emerges from the optimization.
We run one grid per base scene and keep, among its filled cells, the attack with the smallest ego–attacker distance, so each base scene contributes one attack.
The resulting distribution over attack types differs between the two planners (Sec. IV-G ).
Generating a dataset of 50 scenes costs around 30 GPU-hours of search per planner, plus 70 for rendering the survivors (Sec. III-D ). Even a gradient-free search with the real planner in the loop would need one render per candidate, roughly 4,300 GPU-hours. Our surrogate planner, together with the automated search of diverse attacks before any scene is rendered, therefore reduces the search cost substantially.

为了覆盖一个计划员的失败模式, 而不是手取情景类型, 我们运行 优化 在 MAP-Elites [26],
MAP-Elites将一个行为描述符的空间分割成一个网格,并在每个网格细胞中保持物理上最接近自我的攻击.
我们使用两个描述符,联系时间差距和接近角度,在一个5×5 5\时5格。
网格迫使攻击分布在描述空间上,而每个单元格中的攻击类型,如切入或头部方法,则没有指定,从优化中出现.
我们每个基场运行一个网格,并在其填充的细胞中保持最小自负-攻击者距离的攻击,因此每个基场都贡献一个攻击.
由此产生的攻击类型分布在两个规划者之间有所不同(Sec.IV-G.)。
生成一个由50场景组成的数据集,每个规划者花费大约30 GPU小时的搜索时间,加上70场渲染幸存者(Sec. III-D.). 连环中真正的计划员的无梯度搜索也需要每个候选人一个渲染,大约4300GPU小时. 因此,我们的代理规划师,加上在任何场景出现之前自动搜索各种攻击,大大减少了搜索费用。

blocks.en: III-C Solving Safe Escapes
blocks.zh: III-C 解决安全逃逸

blocks.en:
The attack defines the situation; the escape defines the correct response to it.
Holding the attacker’s trajectory fixed, we solve for an escape, the ego trajectory that maximizes clearance to the adversary while staying on-road, avoiding all other agents, remaining kinematically feasible, and keeping the route goal.
No planner participates in this stage.
We run the same MAP-Elites search over the escapes, with a longitudinal descriptor (brake to accelerate) and a lateral one (left to right) on a 5 × 5 5\times 5 grid.
It returns several qualitatively distinct escapes per scene, and the escape with the largest clearance serves as the label.
Any scene where no trajectory clears the adversary by 4 m after a 1 s (12-frame) reaction delay is rejected as unavoidable (15% of attacks). Thus, the planner is never fine-tuned on adversarial situations it could not have survived.
blocks.zh:
攻击定义了局势;越狱定义了正确的反应.
保持攻击者的轨迹固定下来,我们解决了逃逸问题,解决了自我轨迹,这种自我轨迹使敌人在继续前进的同时获得最大程度的许可,避免了所有其他特工,保持了运动上的可行性,并保持了路线目标。
没有计划人员参与这一阶段。
我们运行同样的MAP-Elites搜索在越狱中,有一个纵向描述符(刹车加速),一个横向描述符(左对右)在5×5 5\时5格.
每个场景返回若干个质量上截然不同的越狱,经过最大许可的越狱作为标签。
任何在1秒(12帧)反应延迟后没有轨迹将对手清除4米的场景,都因不可避免的(15%的攻击)而被否决. 因此,规划者从未对本不可能幸存下来的对抗情况进行微调。

blocks.en: III-D Rendering and Fine-Tuning
blocks.zh: 三-D 渲染和精致

blocks.en:
To prepare each surviving scene for rendering, all scene tensors (BEV maps, 3D bounding boxes, camera visibility masks and relative pose embeddings) are recomputed for spatial consistency with the attacker’s trajectory and the ego’s escape.
Each scene is then rendered with MagicDriveV2 [ 4 ] into a six-camera photorealistic clip of 65 frames at 848 × 1600 848\times 1600 per camera.
The base scenes come from the nuScenes train split, so no evaluation scene is used. The renderer itself is trained only on nuScenes.
Rendering takes about 1.4 GPU-hours per scene, around 70 GPU-hours for the 50 scenes of one planner.
We fine-tune the E2E model on the 50 rendered scenes mixed with clean nuScenes, so normal driving is not forgotten.
Perception stays frozen and only parameters inside the planning head f head f_{\mathrm{head}} are updated.
The surrogate is used only to find the 50 scenes and is not deployed.

为了让每个幸存的场景都做好渲染的准备,所有场景的测距仪(BEV地图、三维边框、相机可见度罩和相对的姿势嵌入)都是为了与攻击者的轨迹和自我逃脱的空间一致性而重新计算的。
每个场景随后与MagicDriveV2 [4] 一起制成六摄像头摄影现实主义片段,每台摄像头848×1600 848\times 1600.
基础场景来自nuScenes列车拆分,因此没有使用评价场景. 制造器本身只接受nuScens的培训.
渲染每个场景大约需要1.4GPU小时,一个策划者的50场景大约需要70GPU小时.

blocks.en: IV Experiments
blocks.zh: 四 试验

blocks.en: IV-A Setup
blocks.zh: 四A 设置

blocks.en:
We evaluate two vision-based E2E planners from their released checkpoints, SparseDrive [ 16 ] and DiffusionDrive [ 15 ] . Both planners are evaluated as released, with their own inference pipelines unchanged.
NeuroNCAP [ 3 ] provides closed-loop evaluation in photorealistic collision scenarios of three categories (stationary, frontal, side), reporting a score ( ↑ \uparrow , macro-averaged over categories) and a collision rate ( ↓ \downarrow ).
Challenger [ 2 ] provides open-loop adversarial replay.
Its adversaries are optimized to come close to the ego without colliding, and scenes that the logged ego trajectory cannot traverse safely are discarded.
The logged trajectory serves as ground truth, so the ground-truth ego passes close to the adversary without reacting to it.
Challenger renders with the same generative model as our pipeline, MagicDriveV2, while NeuroNCAP uses neural reconstruction of the original scenes.
Clean nuScenes val [ 27 ] checks that normal driving is preserved.
Fine-tuning runs use three seeds and we report mean and standard deviation.
blocks.zh:
我们评价了两个基于愿景的E2E规划人员,即来自已释放的检查站的SparseDrive[16]和DivusionDrive[15]。 两名规划者被评价为释放,他们自己的推论管道不变.
NeuroNCAP [3] 提供了三种类型(静止、正面、侧面)的光现实碰撞情景中的闭路评价,报告一个分数(XQ ) 和一个碰撞率(XX ) 。
挑战者[2]提供开放式的对战重播.
它的对手被优化到接近自我而不相撞,记录的自我轨迹无法安全穿越的场景被抛弃.
记录下来的轨迹是地面真理,因此地面真理的自我向对手走去,却没有作出反应。

清洁nuScens val [27] 检查正常驾驶是否保存.

blocks.en:
We compare against three data-generation baselines.
The first is recovery-based augmentation inspired by SimScale [ 8 ] , where ego trajectories are perturbed within the nuScenes vocabulary and recovery trajectories are retrieved from a large human-driven trajectory bank via pose-matching.
The second is rule-based, which places scripted stationary and oncoming adversaries on the ego’s route, with escape labels produced by a CEM-Diffusion expert. It is safety-critical by design but blind to the planner.
The third is Challenger-style, which runs Challenger’s own generation on 50 nuScenes train scenes. Its adversaries are optimized to pass close to the ego without colliding, and the logged ego trajectory serves as label, so the data is adversarial but neither aimed at a planner nor paired with an evasive label.
All three baselines use MagicDriveV2 [ 4 ] for video synthesis and receive the same budget of 50 scenes and the same fine-tuning recipe as ours.
So the comparison isolates the scenario design strategy rather than the renderer.
blocks.zh:
我们比较了三个数据生成基线。
首先是受Simscale[8]启发的基于恢复的增强,其中自负轨迹在nuScens词汇中受到干扰,恢复轨迹通过姿势比对从大型人类驱动的轨迹库中检索.
其二是基于规则的,将脚本固定的和即将到来的对手放在自我的路线上,由CEM-Difusion专家制作的逃生标签. 这是安全的关键 设计,但盲从规划者。
第三个是挑战者风格,在50个nuScenes列车场景上运行挑战者自己的一代. 它的对手被优化到接近自我而不相撞,所记录的自我轨迹起到标签的作用,因此数据是对抗性的,但既不针对计划者,也不与回避标签搭配.
所有三个基线都使用MagicDriveV2[4]进行视频合成,并获得与我们相同的50场景和微调配方的预算.
因此比较将情景设计策略隔离,而不是渲染器.

blocks.en:
When an E2E model collides with an adversarial agent, we ask whether the agent was undetected or detected and mishandled. We decompose every NeuroNCAP episode of the unmodified (stock) DiffusionDrive by whether its own detections tracked the adversary before the collision. We count the adversary as detected when recall at 5–35 m is at least 0.5.
Recall is computed on the detections the planner actually consumes, at the model’s native operating point with no additional confidence threshold.
Table I shows the result.
Detection is reliable in every category, and in 95.9% of the collision episodes the adversary was detected, while pure perception failures account for only 4.1% of them. SparseDrive decomposes the same way, with 95.8% of its collisions occurring while the threat was detected.
The per-scenario pattern sharpens the diagnosis, as stationary threats are mostly handled properly, frontal interactions are crashed more often than avoided, and side scenarios collide in half of all episodes despite the best recall of the three.
The diagnosis does not hinge on the recall threshold, as sweeping it from 0.3 to 0.7 moves the detected-and-crashed share from 97.0% to 92.5% on SparseDrive and 97.8% to 89.3% on DiffusionDrive, while episodes that crash with the threat undetected never exceed 3.1% of all episodes.
Detection also holds at close range, with recall rising from 0.84 beyond 15 m to 0.91 within 15 m on DiffusionDrive and from 0.84 to 0.90 on SparseDrive.
The bottleneck is therefore planning, which motivates freezing perception and fine-tuning only the planning layers.

假象模式使诊断更加清晰,因为固定的威胁大多得到妥善处理,前部的相互作用比避免的更频繁地坠毁,尽管三部曲中最出色的召回,但侧面的情景在全部事件中有一半碰撞.

blocks.en: IV-C Main Results

blocks.en:
Fig. 3 shows two of the generated scenes, one per planner, a daytime in-path attack aimed at DiffusionDrive and a night front-brake attack aimed at SparseDrive. Each scene is rendered across all six cameras with the attack and its solved escape traced in BEV.
In addition, Table II gives the quantitative results.
Our scenes roughly halve the closed-loop collision rate of both planners, 28.0% to 12.2% on SparseDrive and 37.5% to 19.2% on DiffusionDrive. Every individual seed improves the stock planner.
The per-scenario scores locate the gain.
Side collisions, the hardest category for both stock planners and the one our failure analysis flagged, improve by about 1.5 points on each, the largest gain of any category.
Frontal improves more modestly and remains the hardest category after fine-tuning.
Stationary scores, already the highest category for both planners, increase further, and SparseDrive reaches the maximum score of 5.0.
Normal driving is largely preserved. The nuScenes collision rate is unchanged on SparseDrive (0.088 vs. 0.094) and slightly lower on DiffusionDrive (0.071 vs. 0.079), and the nuScenes L2 is at most 0.06 higher than that of the stock planner (0.668 vs. 0.609 for SparseDrive, 0.580 vs. 0.574 for DiffusionDrive).
On open-loop Challenger, our collision rate is lower than that of the stock planner on both planners, while all three baselines score better on DiffusionDrive.
The larger L2 is expected, since the Challenger ground truth does not react to the adversary (Sec. IV-A ) while our fine-tuned planners do.

blocks.en:
Our model-aware data is also the best row in both planner blocks, ahead of all three baselines on both score and collision rate.
Recovery data lowers the collision rate from 28.0% to 23.8% on SparseDrive and from 37.5% to 34.7% on DiffusionDrive, a gain of 4.2 and 2.8 points against 16 to 18 points with our data. So photorealistic augmentation that varies the ego’s own trajectory, without an adversarial vehicle, gives only a small gain.
Designing adversarial interactions helps, but neither scripted nor untargeted threats are sufficient.
Rule-based scenes correspond to two of NeuroNCAP’s three categories, yet their collision rate is 17.9% on SparseDrive and 34.3% on DiffusionDrive, against 12.2% and 19.2% with our data, 15 points lower on DiffusionDrive.
The difference is that our attacks are optimized against the planner’s own head and cover the attack types at which that planner actually fails, rather than the types a script prescribes.
Challenger-style scenes, adversarial but aimed at no planner and labeled with the non-reacting logged trajectory, lower SparseDrive’s collision rate to 19.1% and leave DiffusionDrive at 38.8%, no better than stock. The same data gives the best Challenger L2 on both planners and the best Challenger collision rate on DiffusionDrive. Open-loop Challenger metrics therefore do not track closed-loop safety on these planners.

Table III compares three escape labels on the same rule-based scenes: the CEM-Diffusion expert, a brake-always label, and our solved escape.
The solved escape has the highest mean closed-loop score and the lowest collision rate, but its margin over brake-always is small.
Brake-always comes close in closed-loop because, with a single adversary and no cross traffic, stopping usually avoids the collision.
The three labels differ clearly on Challenger.
Brake-always has the highest Challenger collision rate, since the label must provide an evasive path rather than a stop.
CEM-Diffusion has the lowest Challenger collision rate and L2 but the lowest closed-loop score.
Even with our label, rule-based scenes remain below our scenes in Table II (3.939 vs. 4.394); that difference is the contribution of the model-aware attacker.

blocks.zh: 四 -E是代理忠实?

blocks.en:
The surrogate does not need to reproduce the planner in every situation.
Its purpose is to find the scenes in which the planner fails.
We therefore evaluate two properties.
The first is how far π ^ \hat{\pi} deviates from the planner, relative to how far the planner deviates from ground truth.
The second is how reliably a collision predicted by π ^ \hat{\pi} corresponds to a collision of the real planner.
Table IV reports both on nuScenes val, using real images only, because on rendered scenes the comparison would mix adapter error with any drift of the planner’s features c c on synthetic pixels.

其目的是寻找规划者失败的场景.
因此,我们评价两个财产。
第一,相对于规划者偏离地面真相的程度,规划者偏离规划者有多远。

On the first property, π ^ \hat{\pi} deviates from its planner by about as much as the planner deviates from ground truth, 1.02 times that deviation for SparseDrive and 1.12 times for DiffusionDrive.
On the second, we compare collision incidence , which counts a sample as colliding if any predicted timestep collides.
Incidence is a per-sample quantity and differs from the per-timestep collision rate of Table II .
A collision predicted by π ^ \hat{\pi} corresponds to a real collision with precision 0.603 on SparseDrive and 0.673 on DiffusionDrive, against base rates near 1.5%, i.e., 38 and 51 times the base rate.

For a scene generator, low recall is acceptable, since a missed failure mode only reduces coverage.
On the rendered attack scenes themselves, the stock planner, which has never seen them, collides with the attacker in 32 of 50 SparseDrive scenes and 26 of 50 DiffusionDrive scenes. Scenes the stock planner survives still supply a corrective label, since the solved escape maximizes clearance.

blocks.en:
If the surrogate’s gradients carry planner-specific information, data generated against planner A A should help A A more than it helps B B .
Table V shows the full two-by-two comparison, in which each planner is fine-tuned on its own scenes and on the scenes of the other planner, with 3 seeds per entry.
We call the difference between the own-data score and the cross-data score the targeting premium .
Both premiums are positive.
Every own-data seed scores higher than every cross-data seed on both planners.
The premiums nonetheless differ, + 0.18 +0.18 for SparseDrive against + 0.56 +0.56 for DiffusionDrive.
In terms of collision rate, DiffusionDrive trained on SparseDrive’s scenes keeps only 6.7 of the 18.3-point reduction it obtains on its own scenes.

blocks.en:
Fig. 4 shows the distribution of attack types found against each planner.
The attacks against DiffusionDrive concentrate on cut-ins with almost no head-on threats, while those against SparseDrive are spread over cut-ins, head-on and front-brake.
Since every attack is optimized against one planner’s head, attacks of the same type are also expected to differ between the two planners.
The transfer result reflects this, since the scenes found through each surrogate help that surrogate’s own planner most, which requires that the gradients behind those scenes encode failure modes specific to that planner.
A planner-independent proxy would not produce this asymmetry.

由于每次攻击都是针对一个计划者头部进行优化,因此预计两个计划者之间同样类型的攻击也会有所不同.
转移结果反映了这一点,因为通过每个代孕者发现的场景最有助于代孕者自己的规划师,这就要求这些场景背后的梯度编码该规划师特有的故障模式.
计划员独立代理不会产生这种不对称.

blocks.en: IV-G Emergent Diversity
blocks.zh: 新出现的多样性

blocks.en:
The pipeline does not specify scenario types, yet six attack types emerge from the single collision objective (Fig. 4 ).
We assign each attack to a type with a fixed geometric rule based on the adversary’s position and heading relative to the ego at the moment of first contact and during the approach.
The proportions of the types differ between the two planners.
DiffusionDrive’s concentration on cut-ins reflects a weakness of that planner rather than a lack of diversity in the search, since the same search against SparseDrive produces a wider spread.
The escapes are similarly varied and include braking, holding speed, swerving, and accelerating past the adversary, with several qualitatively distinct valid escapes per scene on average.
The main results use only the escape with the largest clearance; the remaining escapes are left for future multi-label training.
blocks.zh:
管道没有具体说明情景类型,然而从单一碰撞目标(图4)中出现了6种攻击类型。
根据对手在第一次接触时和接触期间所处的位置和所处位置,我们把每一次攻击都指定为有固定几何规则的类型。
这两种类型的比例在两个规划者之间有所不同。
因为针对SparseDrive的同样的搜索会产生更广泛的传播,
越狱情况同样多种多样,包括刹车、握住速度、转弯和加速越过对手,平均每场有几次质量上截然不同的有效越狱。
主要结果只使用最大规模的放行;其余的放行留待日后的多标签训练.

blocks.en: V Limitations
blocks.zh: 五 限制

blocks.en:
The first limitation is breadth.
Our evidence covers two planners, so the targeting premium is measured at two points only, and a third architecture would be needed to confirm the trend.
The renderer also restricts us to nuScenes-based planners, and we evaluate on a single closed-loop simulator.
NeuroNCAP’s neural rendering differs from the generative renderer behind our training data, so the gains are not specific to one renderer, but evaluation on further simulators would strengthen this claim.
The second limitation is depth. DiffusionDrive’s surrogate has a recall of 0.544 on that planner’s real collisions (Table IV ), so it misses roughly half of them, and the attacks we find are a subset of the attacks that would succeed against the real planner. The measured premium is therefore a lower bound on what a better surrogate would expose.
The third limitation is the scope of the scenes.
Each scene contains a single adversarial vehicle and no vulnerable road users. We plan to extend the search to multiple adversaries and to vulnerable road users in the future.
blocks.zh:
第一个限制是宽度。
我们的证据包括两个规划者,因此目标溢价只用两个点来衡量,需要第三个结构来证实这一趋势。
渲染器还把我们限制在基于nuScenes的规划器上,我们评价一个单一的闭路模拟器.
NeuronNCAP的神经渲染与我们训练数据背后的基因渲染器不同,因此增益不只局限于一个渲染器,但对进一步模拟器的评价会强化这种说法.
第二个限制是深度。 DivusionDrive 的代孕者在计划者的真正碰撞(表四)上召回了0.544,因此它忽略了其中大约一半,而我们发现的攻击是攻击真正计划者的一个子集。 因此,衡量的溢价对于一个更好的代孕者会暴露出什么影响较小。
第三个限制是场景的范围.
每个场景都包含单辆对抗车,没有易受伤害的道路使用者. 我们计划在今后将搜索范围扩大到多个对手和易受伤害的道路使用者。

blocks.en: Two problems remain open. Frontal scenarios remain the hardest category after fine-tuning. We also train on one escape per scene although the solver produces several, and training with multiple labels per scene is left for future work.
blocks.zh: 两个问题仍未解决。 经过微调后,前期情况仍然是最困难的类别。 我们还每个场景训练一次越狱,虽然解题者会制作若干次,每个场景训练有多个标签,留待未来工作.

blocks.en: VI Conclusion
blocks.zh: 六 结论

blocks.en:
This paper began with a failure analysis of current E2E models.
Decomposing closed-loop collisions showed that end-to-end planners detect the threat in the large majority of collisions but fail to respond to it. The failures are thus mainly a planning problem and not a perception problem, and the missing safety-critical training data must target planning.
The obstacle to generating such data against a specific planner is that a vision-based planner consumes images, and a video renderer inside an optimization loop is computationally infeasible.
Distilling the planner into a differentiable surrogate built from its own frozen planning head, but operating on BEV inputs instead of images, removes this obstacle.
With the renderer outside the optimization loop, gradients are cheap and the attacks are specific to one planner.
blocks.zh:
本文首先对目前的E2E模型进行了故障分析.
分解闭路碰撞表明,端对端规划者在绝大多数碰撞中检测到这种威胁,但未能应对. 因此,失败主要是规划问题,而不是感知问题,缺失的安全关键培训数据必须针对规划。
对照特定规划者生成此类数据的障碍在于,基于视觉的规划者会消耗图像,而优化循环中的视频渲染器在计算上不可行.
将规划师分解成一个与自己冷冻的规划头不同的替代物,但使用BEV输入而不是图像操作,消除了这一障碍.
随着渲染器在优化循环之外,梯度是便宜的,攻击是针对一个规划者的.

blocks.en:
Fifty such scenes per planner, each pairing an optimized attack with a safe escape label, roughly halve the closed-loop collision rate of two vision-based planners while normal driving is largely preserved, at around 30 GPU-hours of search per planner.
The transfer experiment shows that this gain depends on the planner the scenes were generated for.
Each planner improves most on the scenes generated against itself, on every seed, and DiffusionDrive keeps only about a third of its collision-rate reduction when trained on scenes generated against SparseDrive.
This asymmetry is consistent with the method.
Safety-critical training data is therefore planner-specific, and generating it against the planner’s own surrogate is an efficient way to obtain it.
blocks.zh:
每个计划员50场这样的场景,每场将一个最优化的攻击与安全逃生标签对齐,大约将两个基于视觉的规划员的闭路碰撞率减半,而正常的驾驶则基本保持下来,每计划员搜索大约30GPU小时.
转移实验显示,这种收益取决于所生成的场景的规划者.
每个规划师在反自身生成的场景上,在每个种子上改进得最多,当接受针对SparseDrive生成的场景的训练时,DiffunusionDrive只保留了大约三分之一的碰撞率降低.
这种不对称与方法一致.
因此,安全关键培训数据是规划人员特有的,根据规划人员自己的代孕生成数据是获得这些数据的有效途径。
